Otolaryngology · published research

Rhinosinusitis

An exact-category rabbit study reported lower tissue inflammation, but CT opacity and cytokine changes were not statistically significant. These findings are preclinical and do not establish patient benefit.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

An exact-category rabbit study reported lower tissue inflammation, but CT opacity and cytokine changes were not statistically significant. These findings are preclinical and do not establish patient benefit.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact Respiratory system > Rhinosinusitis category contains ten titles: eight human reports, one meta-analysis, and one rabbit study. An additional sham-controlled human trial was located by citation search but is absent from this exact category and is counted separately. The records include different disease definitions and light protocols.

Human and clinical evidence

A 2025 meta-analysis included six studies and 162 participants. Pooled symptom scores improved at two weeks, four weeks, and two to six months, but the four-week estimate was highly heterogeneous. CT findings did not change significantly, and headache or fatigue did not show consistent benefit (Park et al. 2025). In a 20-person sham-controlled study, the true-laser group had a larger symptom-score reduction than sham (34.1% versus 5.0%) (Naghdi et al. 2022). By contrast, a 50-person randomized double-blind trial of mixed UV-visible rhinophototherapy found no significant patient or objective outcome advantage over placebo (Dulguerov et al. 2017). A separate 31-person 2024 sham-controlled PBM trial reported improvement in headache, fatigue, and sinus opacification; this report was found outside the exact database inventory (Afify Abdulrashid et al. 2024). These results suggest a possible symptom signal but not consistent objective improvement.

Animal evidence

The category includes one rabbit rhinosinusitis study. It reported reduced tissue inflammation after treatment, while CT opacity and cytokine changes were not statistically significant. The model does not establish a clinical effect in chronic rhinosinusitis.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone in-vitro or ex-vivo publication was identified in the exact category.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

Protocols include intranasal laser treatment and broader UV-visible rhinophototherapy, with different schedules and disease settings. The 2024 outside-inventory trial used 904-nm PBM at eight sinus sites, 2.5 J per site, for 10 minutes across 12 sessions. These parameters should not be generalized to mixed-spectrum treatments or to all rhinosinusitis diagnoses. Symptom scales and imaging endpoints also differ across trials.

Interpretation

Selected studies report short-term symptom relief, but the evidence is heterogeneous and objective imaging outcomes are less consistent. The additional positive 2024 trial increases the evidence base but does not establish durable benefit or a standard protocol.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow for short-term symptom improvement with selected protocols Very low for objective sinus changes and durable disease control
Publications and records10 titles (8 human reports and 1 meta-analysis).

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Clinical findings are mixed. Small sham-controlled studies report symptom improvement, while a randomized UV-visible rhinophototherapy trial was null. A 2025 meta-analysis found pooled symptom changes but no consistent objective CT benefit and substantial heterogeneity. An additional 2024 sham-controlled PBM trial located outside the exact database category also reported improvement. Independent trials should use standardized symptom and imaging outcomes.
